I can count to 20. Then you pick hopscotch or tag.
Ok. I like two picks. Tell me at lunch before we go out.

supports_hidden_facts.evidence_type: A changed playground plan triggers questions about people, timing, and what comes before the activity.
The child accepts play more readily when turns and limited options are set.

pipeline_notes_only: Playground evidence stays behavioral: counting, turn length, two choices, and advance notice.

calendar_event.notes: Library book, purple folder, snack card, sneakers. Ask Mrs. Keller: assembly before math? how many songs? who sits with our table?

The note lists what to bring and questions about sequence, duration, and participants.

messages.text: Coach moved the Sunrise Sprouts field to the one near the tennis courts tonight.
Is it still 6:15? How many minutes in the car? Do I need orange socks or blue?
Still 6:15. About 12 minutes. Blue socks, shin guards, water. I'll show you the map when I get home.
Can we put practice after dinner on my paper so it matches?

supports_hidden_facts.evidence_type: Sunrise Sprouts is repeatedly foregrounded in family coordination.
A changed location prompts questions about time, duration, and required items.
The child wants the evening activity placed into a written sequence.

pipeline_notes_only: Second week soccer change reinforces the same information-seeking pattern without a direct label.

messages.text: Your blue folder says Mrs. Kline's class will meet in Room 14 this morning, not your regular room.
Can you walk with me until the door?
Yes. You can hold my hand in the hallway, and I will wait until you see Aaliyah.
I will stand by you first.

pipeline_notes_only: Single-fact fallback: fragment provides partial behavioral evidence without naming the label.

messages.text: How did Field 3 go?
She stayed close by my side during sign-in and didn't say much when Coach Riley asked names.
Got it. Did she kick once they started?
Yes, after a few minutes. She joined the line when the kids were doing cone taps.
